questionAnswer.question: Why did the child lag behind his parents?
questionAnswer.answer: The child was very young and curious. Every stall — toys, sweets, flowers, rides — caught his attention. He stopped to look at things and, without noticing, slipped away from his parents' side in the busy crowd.

questionAnswer.question: How does the child's attitude to the fair's attractions change in the story?
questionAnswer.answer: At first he is excited and delighted by everything. After he realises he is lost, the same things lose all meaning. Toys and sweets no longer interest him; he only wants his parents. This shows that love and safety matter more than material things.

questionAnswer.question: Describe the child's feelings when he discovers he is lost.
questionAnswer.answer: He feels sudden shock, fear and helplessness. He looks around frantically, runs here and there and begins to cry. The crowd feels strange and unfriendly, and he feels completely alone.

questionAnswer.question: What is the central message of the story?
questionAnswer.answer: The story tells us that a child's greatest need is the love and protection of parents. Toys, sweets and entertainment can please for a moment, but they can never replace the security of being with family.

questionAnswer.question: How does the author create sympathy for the child?
questionAnswer.answer: The author narrates events through the child's eyes, uses simple language and shows his panic, tears and repeated calls for his parents. Readers easily feel his helplessness and sympathise with him.

questionAnswer.question: What role does the crowd play in the story?
questionAnswer.answer: The crowd shows the busy and impersonal side of a public place. It hides the parents from the child's view and makes him feel unnoticed and small. The crowd increases his fear and sense of isolation.

questionAnswer.question: Why did sweets and toys become meaningless for the child?
questionAnswer.answer: When a child feels safe, small pleasures matter. But once he lost his parents, his basic need for safety was threatened. In that fear, no toy or sweet could comfort him.

questionAnswer.question: Do you think the child was careless? Give reasons.
questionAnswer.answer: He was not really careless; he was only innocent and curious like any small child. The attractive stalls drew him away. The story hints that adults should guide and watch young children closely in crowded places.

questionAnswer.question: Write a short character sketch of the child.
questionAnswer.answer: The child is curious, innocent, lively and sensitive. He is easily attracted by colourful things. He is emotionally dependent on his parents and breaks down quickly when separated from them. His honest cry for his parents wins our sympathy.

questionAnswer.question: How does the story show the contrast between joy and fear?
questionAnswer.answer: The beginning is full of bright colours, music and delight. The ending is full of crying and panic. This sharp turn from joy to fear shows how quickly a happy moment can become frightening for a child alone.

questionAnswer.question: What do you learn about parents' role from this story?
questionAnswer.answer: Parents are a child's shelter and comfort. They guide, protect and love without conditions. The story reminds us how important it is for parents to stay alert and for children to stay close in public places.

questionAnswer.question: Is the title "The Lost Child" suitable? Explain.
questionAnswer.answer: Yes. The story revolves around one child who loses his parents in a fair. The title is simple, direct and also stands for the emotional "lostness" of a child without the love and safety of his family.

questionAnswer.question: Which words/images in the story make the fair look attractive?
questionAnswer.answer: Colourful toys, sweet shops, garlands of flowers, ride attractions, music and crowds create a lively picture. These images appeal to the senses of sight, smell and sound and help readers imagine the fair.

questionAnswer.question: What would you do if you got lost in a crowded place?
questionAnswer.answer: I would stay calm, stand in one safe place and not follow strangers. I would ask a police officer, a shopkeeper or a woman with children for help and tell them my parents' names and phone number.

questionAnswer.question: How did Toto come to Grandfather's private zoo?
questionAnswer.answer: Grandfather saw a monkey with a tonga-driver and felt drawn to it. He bought the little monkey for five rupees and named him Toto. Toto thus became the newest member of Grandfather's collection of pets.

questionAnswer.question: In what sense was Toto "pretty"?
questionAnswer.answer: Toto was small, sleek and lively. His bright eyes shone with mischief under deep-set eyebrows. His quick movements and cheeky expressions made him attractive, even though his behaviour was far from gentle.

questionAnswer.question: Why was Toto kept in a closet at first?
questionAnswer.answer: Grandfather knew Grandmother would not welcome a monkey in the house. So he hid Toto in a small closet. But Toto's naughty nature made it impossible to keep him secret for long.

questionAnswer.question: Why did Grandfather take Toto to Saharanpur, and how?
questionAnswer.answer: Toto had already begun to cause trouble at home, so Grandfather decided to keep him closer. He carried Toto in a large canvas kit-bag on the train journey to Saharanpur.

questionAnswer.question: Why did the ticket collector call Toto a dog?
questionAnswer.answer: Toto had popped his head out of the bag and grinned at the collector. Grandfather had no ticket for a monkey, and the rules had no category for monkeys. The collector decided to treat Toto as a dog and charged accordingly.

questionAnswer.question: How does Toto take a bath?
questionAnswer.answer: Toto enjoyed a warm bath. He would sit in the tub, splash water, rub himself and behave almost like a child. His bath time showed his human-like habits and his love of fun.

questionAnswer.question: How did Toto almost boil himself alive?
questionAnswer.answer: Toto climbed into a kettle of water kept on the fire. As the water warmed, he enjoyed it at first, but when it got too hot he popped his head out. Luckily, he was rescued before serious harm happened.

questionAnswer.question: Describe the pullao incident.
questionAnswer.answer: Toto, hungry and bold, snatched the dish of pullao and escaped through a window. He had no fear of Grandmother's anger. The incident shows how impossible it was to keep him disciplined.

questionAnswer.question: How did Grandmother react to Toto?
questionAnswer.answer: Grandmother disliked Toto's destructive habits. She was shocked when she found him stuffing himself with food, and Toto threw a plate at her. Her reaction showed that the household could not tolerate a monkey.

questionAnswer.question: Why did Grandfather finally sell Toto back?
questionAnswer.answer: Toto's mischief had grown too much — damaged clothes, food thefts and chaos. Grandfather realised a house is no place for a wild monkey, so he found the tonga-driver and sold Toto back for three rupees.

questionAnswer.question: Give a character sketch of Grandfather.
questionAnswer.answer: Grandfather is kind, animal-loving, humorous and patient. He enjoys keeping pets and tolerates their tricks. But he is also practical; when Toto becomes impossible, he takes a sensible decision.

questionAnswer.question: Give a character sketch of Toto.
questionAnswer.answer: Toto is clever, agile, curious and mischievous. He imitates humans and loves food and fun. Though lovable, he is also stubborn and destructive. His behaviour proves his wild nature.

questionAnswer.question: What is the humour in the story?
questionAnswer.answer: The humour lies in Toto's funny actions — grinning at the ticket collector, bathing like a child, sitting in a kettle, running off with a pullao dish. The writer's light tone adds to the fun.

questionAnswer.question: What does the story teach about keeping wild animals as pets?
questionAnswer.answer: Wild animals have natural instincts and need freedom. They cannot adapt to human homes. Keeping them as pets causes trouble for both humans and animals.

questionAnswer.question: Is the title "The Adventures of Toto" suitable?
questionAnswer.answer: Yes. The story is a series of exciting and funny incidents involving Toto — from his purchase to his return. "Adventures" suits his series of daring tricks, and the monkey is the central figure.

questionAnswer.question: In what way was Iswaran an asset to Mahendra?
questionAnswer.answer: Iswaran cooked, managed the household and accompanied Mahendra to every new posting without complaint. In the evening he entertained Mahendra with exciting stories. This made Mahendra's lonely life comfortable and cheerful.

questionAnswer.question: Why did Mahendra not miss a TV in his quarters?
questionAnswer.answer: Not a day passed without Iswaran telling some tale. His stories were lively and full of suspense, so Mahendra found them more entertaining than television.

questionAnswer.question: Describe Iswaran's tusker story.
questionAnswer.answer: Iswaran claimed that he faced a mighty tusker and dealt with it bravely. He told it with drama, pauses and gestures. Whether true or not, it kept Mahendra amused and curious.

questionAnswer.question: What is Mahendra's opinion about ghosts at the beginning?
questionAnswer.answer: Mahendra, a practical man, says ghosts are only figments of imagination. He tells Iswaran that such stories are nonsense and have no basis in reality.

questionAnswer.question: How did Iswaran influence Mahendra even though Mahendra was rational?
questionAnswer.answer: Iswaran's ghost story was told in a vivid and convincing way. On the full-moon night, Mahendra's mind was full of that story. When he heard a moan and saw a shadow, his belief in logic weakened.

questionAnswer.question: Narrate the ghost story told by Iswaran.
questionAnswer.answer: Iswaran said a female ghost appeared on full-moon nights around a lonely place. People heard moaning and saw a figure. The story created a spooky atmosphere that stayed in Mahendra's mind.

questionAnswer.question: What happened on the full-moon night?
questionAnswer.answer: Mahendra woke up hearing a moaning sound nearby and saw a shadow outside the window. He was frightened and unable to explain the experience logically.

questionAnswer.question: How does the story end?
questionAnswer.answer: The next morning Iswaran casually asks Mahendra about the night. Mahendra is shaken and his confidence in his own reasoning is gone. The ending leaves readers amused yet thoughtful.

questionAnswer.answer: Yes. He uses suspense, drama, humour and imagination. He builds interest, stops at the right moment and makes listeners curious. He also adapts stories to his audience.

questionAnswer.question: What are the qualities of a good storyteller?
questionAnswer.answer: A good storyteller has imagination, a clear voice, humour, timing and the ability to build suspense. He also knows his audience and keeps them involved till the end.

questionAnswer.question: Give a character sketch of Mahendra.
questionAnswer.answer: Mahendra is a practical, hardworking and logical person. He values reason and dislikes superstition. Yet, he is human and can be affected by fear when his experience matches a story.

questionAnswer.question: Give a character sketch of Iswaran.
questionAnswer.answer: Iswaran is loyal, cheerful, creative and skilled in cooking. He loves to tell stories and handles Mahendra's needs with care. He is also sly and can mix fact with fiction.

questionAnswer.question: What does the story tell us about the power of words?
questionAnswer.answer: Words can create strong images and emotions. A good story can make us believe, laugh or fear. The story shows how words can influence even a logical person.

questionAnswer.question: Can you think of another ending for the story?
questionAnswer.answer: Mahendra could investigate and discover that the noise came from the wind or an animal, and both laugh together. Or Iswaran could reveal he himself played a prank to scare Mahendra.

questionAnswer.question: Why is the title "Iswaran the Storyteller" suitable?
questionAnswer.answer: The story is centred on Iswaran and his tales. Every important event is linked to his storytelling. The title clearly points to his main role and personality.

questionAnswer.question: What was strange about the kingdom the Guru and disciple visited?
questionAnswer.answer: In that kingdom every item, from vegetables to sweets, sold at the same price. There was no difference between good and bad, valuable and worthless. This showed that the people and the ruler did not use common sense.

questionAnswer.question: Why did the disciple want to stay there?
questionAnswer.answer: The disciple loved sweets and found them cheap. He thought life there was easy and pleasant. He ignored the dangers of a place without proper rules.

questionAnswer.question: Why did the Guru decide to leave?
questionAnswer.answer: The Guru understood that a kingdom where everything is treated alike has no justice or wisdom. He warned the disciple but, when the disciple refused to listen, he left alone.

questionAnswer.question: How did the thief die?
questionAnswer.answer: The thief tried to break into a merchant's house by digging through its wall. The poorly built wall collapsed on him and he died on the spot.

questionAnswer.question: How did the king handle the thief's case?
questionAnswer.answer: The king listened to the thief's relatives and decided someone must pay. Without proper enquiry he blamed the merchant, and the blame then passed from person to person.

questionAnswer.question: Describe how the blame passed from one person to another.
questionAnswer.answer: The merchant blamed the builder of the wall. The builder blamed another worker involved, who pointed to a dancer whose movements had distracted him. The dancer blamed the goldsmith who had made her ornaments. In the end, the goldsmith was condemned.

questionAnswer.question: Why was the disciple chosen to be hanged?
questionAnswer.answer: The noose was too big for the thin goldsmith. The king ordered his men to find someone fit for it. They found the plump disciple, and so he was arrested.

questionAnswer.question: How did the Guru save his disciple?
questionAnswer.answer: The Guru returned and whispered to the disciple. He then claimed that whoever was hanged at that moment would go straight to heaven. Both argued to be hanged first. The king heard this and, wanting heaven himself, took the noose.

questionAnswer.question: What does the end of the story show about the king?
questionAnswer.answer: The king was foolish and greedy. He acted without thinking and was fooled by a clever trick. His own foolishness caused his end.

questionAnswer.question: Character sketch of the Guru.
questionAnswer.answer: The Guru is wise, practical and far-sighted. He senses danger in the kingdom early. He uses his intelligence to rescue the disciple at the last moment.

questionAnswer.question: Character sketch of the disciple.
questionAnswer.answer: The disciple is greedy and careless. He ignores his Guru's advice and almost loses his life. But he is also lucky to have a wise teacher.

questionAnswer.question: Why is the story called "In the Kingdom of Fools"?
questionAnswer.answer: The ruler and his people behave foolishly — equal prices for everything, unfair punishments, endless blame games. The title suits a land where common sense is absent.

questionAnswer.question: What lesson do we learn from the story?
questionAnswer.answer: We should use judgement and not blindly follow rules. Wise advice should be respected, and greed can lead to danger.

questionAnswer.question: What does the story say about justice?
questionAnswer.answer: True justice needs careful enquiry and fairness. In this kingdom the king punished at random, which is injustice. The story teaches that a ruler must be wise and just.

questionAnswer.question: How is humour used in the story?
questionAnswer.answer: The humour lies in the absurd blame chain, the fat disciple chosen for the noose and the king hanging himself for heaven. The writer uses exaggeration to make a serious point.

questionAnswer.question: Describe the statue of the Happy Prince.
questionAnswer.answer: The statue stood on a tall column in the city. It was covered with thin gold leaf, had two bright sapphires for eyes and a large red ruby on its sword hilt. People admired it for its beauty.

questionAnswer.question: Why did the Swallow stay behind when his friends flew to Egypt?
questionAnswer.answer: The Swallow had fallen in love with a graceful Reed and delayed his journey. Later he realised the Reed had no love or conversation to offer, so he decided to leave, but stayed to help the Prince.

questionAnswer.question: Why was the Prince crying?
questionAnswer.answer: When he was alive, the Prince knew only joy. After his death, standing on the high column, he could see the misery of his city. Seeing poverty and suffering made him weep.

questionAnswer.question: How did the Swallow help the seamstress?
questionAnswer.answer: At the Prince's request, the Swallow carried the ruby from the sword hilt to a poor seamstress. Her son was ill with fever and she had no money. The Swallow dropped the ruby by her side, and fanned the child to cool his fever.

questionAnswer.question: How did the Prince help the young playwright?
questionAnswer.answer: A young playwright in a cold attic was too weak and hungry to finish his play. The Prince gave one of his sapphire eyes, which the Swallow carried to him. With its price he could buy food and fuel and finish the play.

questionAnswer.question: Who was the little match girl and how was she helped?
questionAnswer.answer: She was a poor girl whose matches had fallen into the gutter, and her father would beat her without money. The Prince gave his second sapphire eye to her so she would be safe.

questionAnswer.question: Why did the Swallow decide to stay with the Prince?
questionAnswer.answer: The Prince had become blind after giving both his eyes. The Swallow felt pity and loyalty and stayed to be his eyes, telling him about the city's sufferings.

questionAnswer.question: How did the Prince use his gold leaf?
questionAnswer.answer: The Prince asked the Swallow to remove the gold leaf, piece by piece, and give it to the poor. Each gift made the children's faces glow and bring cheer to many families.

questionAnswer.question: How did the Swallow die?
questionAnswer.answer: Winter grew bitterly cold and the Swallow had stayed too long. He kissed the Prince goodbye and, weakened by cold, fell dead at his feet.

questionAnswer.question: What happened to the Prince's lead heart?
questionAnswer.answer: When the Swallow died, the Prince's leaden heart snapped in two. This symbolised his love and sorrow at the bird's death.

questionAnswer.question: Why did the mayor and councillors melt the statue?
questionAnswer.answer: They saw only a shabby statue without its gold, ruby and sapphires. They thought it was no longer beautiful and decided to melt it, caring more for appearance than kindness.

questionAnswer.question: What happened to the Prince's heart after melting?
questionAnswer.answer: The furnace melted the statue but not the broken heart. It was thrown on the dust heap near the dead Swallow.

questionAnswer.question: How does the story end?
questionAnswer.answer: God asked an angel to bring the two most precious things of the city. The angel brought the lead heart and the dead bird. God said the bird would sing in His paradise and the Prince would praise Him in His city of gold.

questionAnswer.question: Character sketch of the Happy Prince.
questionAnswer.answer: The Prince is kind, selfless and compassionate. Even though he is a statue, he gives away all his treasures. His love for the poor makes him truly "happy" in the moral sense.

questionAnswer.question: What is the message of the story?
questionAnswer.answer: True happiness lies in helping others. Sacrifice and kindness are more valuable than gold and jewels. The story also criticises people who judge by outer beauty only.

Yeh sachchi ghatna par aadharit hai: Orissa (Odisha) ka super cyclone, October 1999.
- Prashant, ek 19 saal ka ladka, apne gaon Kalikuda se karib 18 km door Ersama ek dost se milne gaya tha. (Saat saal pehle uski maa guzar chuki thi.)

- Wo aaram karne ke bajaye madad mein juta. Usne jawanon aur buzurgon ka group banaya, jo khaana aur raahat ikatthi karne gaya.
- Pehli baar chaar dino ke baad shelter ke logon ko pet bhar khaana mila.
- Prashant ne anaath bachchon ko saath laaya, mahilaon ko food-for-work jaise kaamo mein jodne ki koshish ki.

questionAnswer.question: What havoc did the super cyclone cause in Orissa?
questionAnswer.answer: The cyclone killed thousands of people and destroyed hundreds of villages. Houses were swept away, crops and animals were lost and many families were left homeless. Floods and heavy rain made survival even harder.

questionAnswer.question: Where was Prashant when the cyclone struck?
questionAnswer.answer: Prashant had gone to Ersama, about eighteen kilometres from his village, to spend a day with a friend. In the evening a dark and menacing storm came, trapping him there.

questionAnswer.question: How did Prashant and his friend's family survive the storm?
questionAnswer.answer: They took shelter on the roof of the house. Strong winds and floods raged below, but they held on for two days and nights until the storm subsided.

questionAnswer.question: What did Prashant see after the storm?
questionAnswer.answer: In the morning light he saw a ruined landscape — fallen trees, damaged houses, floating dead bodies of people and animals. The sight shocked him deeply.

questionAnswer.question: Why was it difficult for Prashant to travel back?
questionAnswer.answer: Roads were blocked with debris and covered with water. Bodies and wrecked houses lay everywhere. He had to find his way carefully and walked a long distance in exhaustion and sorrow.

questionAnswer.question: How did Prashant feel on the way to his village?
questionAnswer.answer: He was filled with fear and worry for his family. The sight of destruction made him fear the worst, and he even wept aloud on the way.

questionAnswer.question: How did Prashant find his family?
questionAnswer.answer: On reaching Kalikuda, he found his house gone, then went to the Red Cross shelter. There he anxiously scanned the crowd and found his family alive and safe.

questionAnswer.question: What was the condition of the Red Cross shelter?
questionAnswer.answer: It was crowded with about two thousand five hundred people — wounded, hungry, mourning and frightened. There was little food and no organised help.

questionAnswer.question: How did Prashant arrange food for the shelter?
questionAnswer.answer: He gathered a group of youths and elders. They collected rice and other supplies from the village and cooked for everyone. For the first time in four days the survivors got a full meal.

questionAnswer.question: What did Prashant do for the orphaned children?
questionAnswer.answer: He found that many children had lost their parents. He brought them together, looked after their needs and helped them cope with their grief.

questionAnswer.question: How did Prashant show leadership?
questionAnswer.answer: He did not wait for outside help. He organised youth groups, arranged food, cleaned the shelter and persuaded the women to join work programmes. His courage and calm inspired others.

questionAnswer.question: Do you think Prashant is a good leader? Why?
questionAnswer.answer: Yes. He is brave, responsible and caring. He puts others before himself, makes plans and brings people together. He proves leadership depends on character, not age.

questionAnswer.question: What can young people learn from Prashant?
questionAnswer.answer: Young people can learn to stay calm in a crisis, to help others and to take initiative. Age is no barrier to doing good.

questionAnswer.question: How can people be better prepared for natural disasters?
questionAnswer.answer: By building cyclone shelters, giving early warnings, training volunteers, using safe building materials and keeping emergency supplies ready.

questionAnswer.question: Why is the title "Weathering the Storm in Ersama" suitable?
questionAnswer.answer: "Weathering" means surviving and overcoming. The story is about surviving a real storm and also the emotional storm of loss. Prashant weathers both with courage.

questionAnswer.question: Where and when does the story take place?

questionAnswer.question: Who were Sue and Johnsy?

questionAnswer.question: What did the doctor tell Sue about Johnsy?
questionAnswer.answer: The doctor said Johnsy had only a slim chance to survive. Medicine would help only if she wanted to live. If she lost her will, treatment would be useless.

questionAnswer.question: Why was Johnsy counting the leaves?
questionAnswer.answer: Johnsy had lost hope and believed her life was tied to the leaves on the ivy outside the window. She thought that when the last leaf fell, she would die too.

questionAnswer.question: How did Sue react to Johnsy's belief?
questionAnswer.answer: Sue was worried. She tried to comfort Johnsy, urged her to rest and distracted her by drawing. She also asked Behrman for help as a model.

questionAnswer.question: Describe Behrman.
questionAnswer.answer: Behrman was a sixty-year-old failed painter with an untidy beard. He was bad-tempered but had a soft heart. He always spoke of painting a masterpiece but never did. He cared for Sue and Johnsy like a protector.

questionAnswer.question: How did Behrman react to Johnsy's belief about the leaves?
questionAnswer.answer: He scoffed at her "foolish" idea in anger but felt deep concern. He promised to pose for Sue, secretly planning something to save Johnsy.

questionAnswer.question: What happened on the stormy night?
questionAnswer.answer: A violent wind and icy rain lashed the city all night. Johnsy expected that all leaves would fall. In the morning, though, one leaf still clung to the vine.

questionAnswer.question: How did the last leaf change Johnsy?
questionAnswer.answer: She saw the brave leaf survive the storm and realised she was wrong to wish for death. Her hope returned, she asked for food and began to recover.

questionAnswer.question: What was the secret of the last leaf?
questionAnswer.answer: The leaf was not real. Behrman painted it on the wall with brush and colours on the stormy night. It looked so real that it deceived even Johnsy.

questionAnswer.question: How did Behrman die?
questionAnswer.answer: He had to stay out in the cold and rain to paint the leaf. He caught pneumonia and died in hospital two days later. His sacrifice saved Johnsy's life.

questionAnswer.question: Why is the last leaf called Behrman's masterpiece?

questionAnswer.question: Character sketch of Sue.
questionAnswer.answer: Sue is caring, loyal and practical. She nurses her friend patiently and tries every way to give her hope. Her love shows true friendship.

questionAnswer.question: What does the story teach about hope?
questionAnswer.answer: Hope can be as powerful as medicine. A positive mind helps recovery. The story shows that will to live can win over illness.

questionAnswer.question: Is the title "The Last Leaf" suitable?
questionAnswer.answer: Yes. The last leaf is at the centre of the plot. It symbolises hope, sacrifice and art. The title makes readers curious and fits the story's emotional climax.

questionAnswer.question: How did Zan feel when he joined the new school?
questionAnswer.answer: Zan felt lonely and nervous. His old friends were elsewhere, the school was large and he felt lost in the crowd. He missed being a top student in his small junior school.

questionAnswer.question: How did the fire start?
questionAnswer.answer: On a Sunday afternoon, the fire in the fireplace spread and quickly engulfed the house. Zan and his mother noticed smoke and flames and ran out for safety.

questionAnswer.question: What did Zan's mother do during the fire?
questionAnswer.answer: She picked up a box of precious memories of Zan's father and brought it outside. In panic she dropped it on the grass and rushed back into the burning house.

questionAnswer.question: How did Zan react?
questionAnswer.answer: He was terrified and helpless. He called for the fire service, feared for his mother and cat, and wept bitterly when he saw the house destroyed.

questionAnswer.question: What did Zan lose in the fire?
questionAnswer.answer: He lost his house, clothes, books, belongings and above all his dear cat, which had been like family. The fire took away comfort and memories.

questionAnswer.question: Where did Zan and his mother go after the fire?
questionAnswer.answer: They moved to his grandparents' home, where they got shelter and care while trying to settle again.

questionAnswer.question: How did Zan feel on the next day at school?
questionAnswer.answer: He felt embarrassed and out of place because he had no shoes and wore odd borrowed clothes. He feared that classmates would laugh at him.

questionAnswer.question: How did the school community respond?
questionAnswer.answer: Teachers and classmates offered clothes, notebooks, shoes and kind words. They showed that people care when someone is in trouble.

questionAnswer.question: How did Zan's outlook change after the fire?
questionAnswer.answer: At first he felt alone. After the kindness of his classmates, he felt that he belonged. He realised that people can be warm and that he was not alone.

questionAnswer.question: What happened a month later?
questionAnswer.answer: Zan visited his house, which was being rebuilt, along with new friends. Seeing the new walls rise, he felt his own life was also being rebuilt with hope.

questionAnswer.question: What did the rebuilding of the house symbolise?
questionAnswer.answer: It symbolised healing and new beginnings. As the house was rebuilt, Zan's confidence, friendships and sense of belonging were also built again.

questionAnswer.question: How does the story end?
questionAnswer.answer: Zan is reunited with his cat, which is found safe. He feels whole again and understands what makes a home.

questionAnswer.question: Explain the title "A House Is Not a Home".
questionAnswer.answer: A house is only a building. A home needs love, warmth, friends and family. Zan lost his house but found a home in the care of people around him.

questionAnswer.question: Give a character sketch of Zan.
questionAnswer.answer: Zan is sensitive, thoughtful and brave. He is shy at first but shows resilience. He accepts help with gratitude and learns the value of human relationships.

questionAnswer.question: What lessons does the story teach?
questionAnswer.answer: We learn that kindness can heal pain, that loss can lead to growth, and that family and friends are the real home. We should also help others in distress.

Skvortsov, ek vakeel (lawyer), ek din ghar se nikalta hai to ek phate-purane kapde wala bhikhari, Lushkoff, use rokta hai aur madad maangta hai.
- Wo kehta hai ki wo bekaar, bhukha hai aur use kaam nahi mil raha. Skvortsov use pehchaan leta hai — pehle bhi us bhikhari ne alag kahani sunai thi (ki wo ek vidyarthi hai jo nikala gaya).
- Skvortsov ko dhokha dikhta hai, par wo seedha daantne ke bajaye kehta hai: "Kaam karo, main tumhe lakdi chirne ka kaam deta hoon."
- Bhikhari ghabra jaata hai par maan jaata hai. Skvortsov apni cook Olga ko kehta hai ki bhikhari ko lakdi ke shed mein le jaaye.
- Bhikhari kamzor aur sharaab ka aadi hai. Wo lakdi chirna shuru karta hai, par thak jaata hai.
- Olga use gusse se daant-daant kar kaam karwati hai. Do din tak bhikhari kaam karta hai aur khaata-peeta hai.
- Skvortsov ko dikhta hai ki bhikhari kaam kar sakta hai, par usne pehle kabhi nahi kiya.
- Do saal baad Skvortsov ek theatre mein ek saaf-suthre aadmi se milta hai — wo wahi Lushkoff hai, ab ek chhoti naukri karne wala ek izzatdar aadmi.
- Wo Skvortsov ko dhanyavaad deta hai, par Skvortsov kehta hai ki ye sab Olga ki wajah se hua — Olga ne use sahi raasta dikhaya.
- Seekh: Sachchi madad daya nahi, balki mehnat karne ki prerna hai.

questionAnswer.question: Who were the main characters of the story?
questionAnswer.answer: The main characters are Skvortsov the lawyer, Lushkoff the beggar and Olga the cook. Each plays a role in changing the beggar's life.

questionAnswer.question: How did Lushkoff try to get help from Skvortsov?
questionAnswer.answer: He stopped the lawyer on the road in torn clothes and told a sad story of unemployment and hunger. He hoped to win sympathy and money.

questionAnswer.question: Why did Skvortsov recognise the beggar?
questionAnswer.answer: He had seen the same beggar earlier telling a different story. This showed Lushkoff was dishonest and used false stories to get money.

questionAnswer.question: What offer did Skvortsov make?
questionAnswer.answer: Instead of money, Skvortsov offered work — chopping wood. He wanted the beggar to earn his living and not just beg.

questionAnswer.question: How did Lushkoff react to the offer?
questionAnswer.answer: He was embarrassed and unwilling at first but accepted because he had no choice. His reaction showed he was used to idleness.

questionAnswer.question: Describe Lushkoff's condition when he started the work.
questionAnswer.answer: He was weak, thin and addicted to drink. He struggled to lift the axe and tired quickly, but kept working under Olga's watch.

questionAnswer.question: What role did Olga play in the story?
questionAnswer.answer: Olga took the beggar to the shed and made him work. She scolded him but also fed him. Her firm and caring nature helped him start a new life.

questionAnswer.question: What happened after two days?
questionAnswer.answer: Lushkoff finished the work and was paid. The two days of labour showed him that he could earn an honest living.

questionAnswer.question: How did Skvortsov meet Lushkoff after two years?
questionAnswer.answer: He met him at a theatre, where Lushkoff looked clean and respectable. He had a job and had given up begging.

questionAnswer.question: How did Lushkoff change?
questionAnswer.answer: He changed from an idle, deceitful beggar into a hardworking, self-respecting man. The experience of honest work inspired him to reform.

questionAnswer.question: Why did Skvortsov credit Olga for the change?
questionAnswer.answer: Skvortsov had only offered the job, but Olga personally made him work and showed him the value of effort. Her firm guidance brought the lasting change.

questionAnswer.question: Character sketch of Skvortsov.
questionAnswer.answer: Skvortsov is intelligent and practical. He wants to help but prefers to teach self-reliance. He is humble enough to give credit to Olga.

questionAnswer.question: Character sketch of Lushkoff.
questionAnswer.answer: At first Lushkoff is lazy, dishonest and dependent. Later he becomes hardworking and grateful. His story shows people can change.

questionAnswer.question: What is the message of the story?
questionAnswer.answer: Real help is not charity but encouragement to work and become self-reliant. Honest labour gives dignity and a better future.

questionAnswer.question: Is the title "The Beggar" suitable?
questionAnswer.answer: Yes. The story begins with a beggar and follows his transformation. It focuses on how a beggar becomes an independent man, so the title is apt.
